task.description: REWORK REQUIRED. Your design's SS6 crash-safety-net claim (a task killed by Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) still decrements the ref count via :DOWN, covering a hung invocation) rests on an outer bounding mechanism for invoke/4 that SS3 (public API) and SS4 (numbered algorithm) never actually specify. The validator traced this precisely: your design builds a brand-new Task.Supervisor.async_nolink task under a brand-new ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor, with checkout happening as step 1 INSIDE that task (SS4), but nowhere does the design state (a) who calls Task.yield/2 on this task -- presumably invoke/4 itself, waiting on the task it just spawned, (b) what timeout value that outer wait uses relative to the timeout_ms parameter already threaded into step 4's Wasmex.call_function(pid, export, args, timeout_ms) call, or (c) how a task crash/kill gets converted into the {:error, {:timeout, timeout_ms}} tuple SS3 lists as one of invoke/4's declared return values. This matters because REQ-170's ACTUAL shipped mechanism (lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex:152-222, lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex's own moduledoc, decision 0014 lines 325-327) has TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT timeout paths that your design's SS6 narrative conflates into one: (1) the INNER Wasmex.call_function/4 GenServer.call timeout, which typically fires FIRST and crashes the task on its own, surfacing as the {:exit, reason} branch of the outer Task.yield/2 -- NOT the Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) branch; (2) the OUTER caller's Task.yield/2 bound (a separate, larger timeout_ms), which only fires and calls Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) if the inner GenServer.call timeout somehow doesn't. Your SS6 crash-safety argument -- that ref-count-leak-on-hang is covered by Process.monitor + :DOWN when Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) fires -- needs to explicitly account for BOTH paths, since decision 0014 mandates that WASM reuse PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's own two-layer dispatch pattern (async_nolink -> Task.yield/2 -> Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill)), not silently reinvent it with different plumbing. Fix: explicitly specify in SS3/SS4 which process calls Task.yield/2 on invoke/4's spawned task (most likely invoke/4 itself, mirroring but not necessarily reusing PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's exact call), what timeout value governs that outer wait relative to the already-threaded timeout_ms, and how EACH of the two crash/timeout paths (inner GenServer.call timeout crashing the task vs. outer Task.yield bound firing + Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill)) is classified into invoke/4's declared {:error, {:timeout, timeout_ms}} return -- and confirm your Process.monitor/:DOWN ref-count-release argument in SS6 actually holds for BOTH paths, not just the outer one.
acceptance_criteria: a test holds an invocation open (a guest blocked in a controllable host call), activates a new module version DURING it, and asserts the held invocation completes normally against the OLD version's observable behaviour -- WASM-14's own acceptance criterion, with the overlap real rather than sequential
the same test asserts an invocation started AFTER the activation observes the NEW version's behaviour, so both halves of WASM-14 are proven in one overlapping scenario
the two module versions used are observably different in output, so the test can distinguish which version served an invocation rather than merely completing
a test asserts the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes, not at activation time

a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
